Settings
Theme
Brass, green felt and ivory — the default.
Custom theme colors
Starts from Tournament Felt — pick any to override it, or reset to go back to the defaults. Combine with your own background image and the glass effect below to build your own look.
Piece outline
The outline drawn around each piece, separate from its fill color above. Turn it off for a flat, outline-free look, or pick a color to override it.
Piece style
The classic Staunton set.
Square outlines
A hairline around every square. Applies to every drill.
Arrow colors
The color of the arrows and highlights you draw on a board.
Liquid glass titles
50%
Frosted panel behind each drill title, with a specular sweep on hover. The Bauhaus theme prints them flat instead.
Game intro
The opening over the board. Every theme shows the black-and-white VS screen, with “Round one, fight,” when an online game begins, against a player or the bot. Uptown Express opens its subway doors instead, for any game and when a Puzzles session or a Puzzle Rush starts. Off skips the screen; the start sound still plays.
Line signs
Uptown Express: the board’s ranks and files as subway line signs, each in its line’s colour. Off keeps plain coordinates.
Background
Default
Bauhaus, Game Boy, Drive-Thru and Rosé come with their own artwork, which can be switched to the theme’s pattern. Or upload your own image, saved per theme. A scrim is laid over it so text stays readable. Kept on this device only.
Analysis board cards
The cards around the board when you review a game. Turn one off to hide it; the cards left in its column take its room. With the Engine card off the engine still runs when it’s on (L turns it on or off).
Sound Effects
Volume 100%
Move, capture, check, and checkmate sounds — the same set as Repertoire Lab's board.
Custom Sounds
Even out volume
Plays every uploaded sound at the level of the sound it replaces.
Saved per theme — each one keeps its own set, so switching Theme above switches which sounds play too. Replace any sound with your own audio file, under 3MB each — anything left alone uses the theme's default, or the built-in sound if it doesn't have one. Saved on this device only.
Lichess Connection
Not connected
Needed for the Puzzles drill, Play Online, Play Bot, and the friends-online list. Create a token at lichess.org/account/oauth/token with puzzle:read, puzzle:write, board:play, challenge:write, bot:play, follow:read, study:read and study:write — puzzle:write because Lichess only serves a new puzzle once the last one's result is reported, board:play to seek and play real games, challenge:write and bot:play to start a game against the Lichess AI, follow:read to see which of your followed players are online, study:read and study:write to keep your Saved Puzzles in private Lichess studies so they appear on all your devices. Paste it here — it's saved on this device only, in this browser's local storage, and is never written into the app itself. These features need a real network origin (this app's Netlify URL, or a locally-saved copy) — the hosted claude.ai preview link's security sandbox blocks outside network calls entirely.

Knight's Tour

A bare board, one knight. No clock pressure — just click a lit square to hop there. A running stopwatch tracks your time for bragging rights only.
Mode
Reach the marked square in the fewest hops possible — the board tells you exactly how many.
Position complexity
Easy: 1–2 hops. Medium: 3–4. Hard: 5–6, the longest distance a knight can be from anything on this board.

Drill 06

Sneaky Checks

Your king is in double check, so it has to move — nothing can block two checks at once. Three steps: see the checks, work out which escapes are traps, then commit to the one square that ends the attack.
Three phases
1 Right-click-drag a yellow arrow from each checking piece onto the king
2 Then a purple arrow from the king to every flight square that runs into another check
3 Finally walk the king to the square that's left
Every flight square looks frightening. On all but one the attacker still has a check waiting and the assault rolls on. The right square leaves them with nothing — the attack is simply over.
Position complexity
Harder boards put more attackers around your king, so more escape squares run into a follow-up check.
Show how many checks
A scaffold worth dropping once the pattern lands — with it off you have to trust your own count.

Drill 12

Whose Line Is It Anyway?

A memory and calculation workout. The board shows where the pieces started and never changes. Mark which pieces guard which and press Check; then a move is called out — picture it on top of everything before it and mark the guards again. It trains you to hold the board in your head and see what's guarding what.
How a line runs
1Mark every guard in the start position, then Check
2A move is called out, like Bb5. The board stays put — play it in your head
3Mark the guards in the new position. Next move calls the one after
A piece guards another if it covers that piece's square, so it could take back there. Lines stop at the first piece in the way, counting pieces only you can see; knights jump; a pawn covers the two squares diagonally ahead. The king counts both ways: it guards the pieces on the eight squares around it, and any piece that covers the king's square guards the king. A move can land where the board still shows a piece — that piece has already left.
List shows the moves called so far. Hold Peek to see the board in your head, or tap it to keep it showing — that position then can't count as first try. Reveal shows the answer and the real board.
Pieces
Four is the classic set: queen, rook, bishop and knight. Three drops one of them; five adds a king or a pawn; six has one of every piece.
Moves per line
Endless keeps calling moves with no List or Peek. A wrong Check or a Reveal costs one of three lives, and your deepest line is saved for each piece count.
Clock
seconds per move
Untimed counts up so you can see your pace. With a clock, running out reveals the answer.
Keys
Q RQueen guards rook (any two piece letters: K Q R B N P)
EnterCheck, then Next move
SpaceHold to Peek · L List · Backspace Clear · X flip
On a touch screen, tap a chip: in the queen's row, the rook chip means the queen guards the rook.

    Drill 13

    Static Boards

    A memory workout. A position appears on the board: hold it in your head, press Rebuild, and the board empties. Put every piece back on its square, then Check work. It trains you to take in the whole board at once and keep it.
    How a board runs
    1Study the position for as long as you like, or against a clock
    2Rebuild: the board empties and the pieces wait beside it. Drag each one to its square, or tap a piece, then a square
    3Check work: green is right, red is on the wrong square, and a faded piece shows where one belongs
    Two pieces of the same kind are interchangeable: either white knight can go on either knight square. Give up shows the board you studied; Try again brings the same position back to study.
    Pieces
    Both kings are always on the board, plus pieces from both sides. Ladder starts at three and adds a piece after every perfect rebuild; three misses end the climb, and your best is saved.
    Board area
    Half keeps every piece inside four ranks or four files, Quarter inside one 4x4 corner, and the rest of the board is dimmed. A smaller area packs the pieces closer together.
    Study time
    Until I'm ready waits for Rebuild. With a clock, the board empties by itself when it runs out.
    Start the pieces
    Scattered drops every piece on a wrong square of the board, and you move each one home.
    Keys
    SpaceRebuild once you have the position
    e7Type a square to put the picked piece there (Tab to a piece in the tray; Enter picks it). With nothing picked, it picks up the piece on that square
    EnterCheck work, then Next board · Backspace back to the tray · Esc let go · T try again

    Drill 07 · Arcade

    Endgame Reflexes

    A passed pawn is running. Draw the square from the pawn to its promotion square — if the defending king is inside it, the pawn is caught. That's the whole skill, and it should be instant. The other king is parked too far away to matter.
    How to play
    C Call caught — the king runs it down
    P Call promotes — the pawn gets there first
    Three lives. Every correct call builds your combo and speeds the clock up. Miss one and the board draws you the square.
    Margin
    How close the race is. Hard decides every position by a single tempo — the ones you actually misjudge.
    Starting clock
    seconds per position
    The clock tightens as your combo climbs — down to 1.2s, or your own number if you set it faster.

    Drill 01 · Arcade

    Kiss of Death

    A white queen is touching the black king — a contact check. The only squares the king can ever run to are the two diagonally behind it, away from the queen. If those are covered and the queen is defended, it's mate. Call it before the bar empties.
    How to play
    M Call mate — the king has nowhere to go
    E Call escape, then click the square it runs to
    Three lives. Every correct call builds your combo and speeds the clock up. The board tells you why whenever you miss.
    Position complexity
    Harder boards add decoy pieces — including defenders whose line is quietly blocked.
    Starting clock
    seconds per position
    The clock tightens as your combo climbs — down to 1.2s, or straight to your own number if you set it faster than that.

    Drill 02 · Arcade

    Ghosts!

    A position flashes for under a second and then it's gone. Some are real threats. Some just look like one — a fork the knight can't reach, a pin on the wrong diagonal, a "hanging" piece with a defender standing right behind it. The question isn't "can you solve this." It's "does this deserve your attention." Answer wrong by calling a ghost real, and it costs you more than answering slow.
    How to play
    SPACE Call threat — something real is happening
    — Do nothing — it's a ghost, let it pass
    Call a real threat and you'll have a moment to tap where the danger actually is — not to solve it, just to prove you saw it. Three lives. The window shrinks as your streak grows.
    Packs
    Knight forks, hanging pieces, and bishop/rook/queen lines — each with a real version and a ghost that shares its shape. Turn any off to drill one pattern at a time. More packs are coming.
    Starting pace
    seconds per flash
    New to the pattern? Give yourself a few seconds to start — every window still tightens toward 0.5s as your streak climbs, no matter where it starts.

    Drill 04 · Arcade

    CheckStorm

    Your king is in check. The question isn't "what's the best move" — it's "what's even on the table." Tag every response type that's actually available. A knight check makes block impossible before you calculate anything; that has to become instant.
    How to play
    C Capture — something can take the checking piece
    P Protect — a piece can block the line
    R Run — the king has a safe square to step to
    There can be more than one right answer — tag every option that's really there, not just the best one. Hit ENTER (or Lock it in) the moment you're sure, or just let the clock run out and whatever you've tagged is your answer. Three lives. The window shrinks as your streak grows.
    Starting pace
    seconds per check
    New to this one? Give yourself more time to start — every window still tightens as your streak climbs, no matter where it starts.

    Drill 03 · Arcade

    King's Ground

    Kings can never stand next to each other — so the eight squares around your king are squares the enemy king simply cannot enter. That rule is the whole game. Stand in the right place and the enemy has to walk around you. You'll feel opposition and shouldering long before anyone names them.
    Mission
    Hold the line. The enemy king is trying to reach the bottom row — keep him out until the clock runs out.
    How to play
    WASD Move your king — arrow keys work too
    SPACE Push the pawn (Escort only)
    One action per beat. Miss the beat and you forfeit the turn — the enemy still moves. Forcing him onto a longer route scores DETOUR.
    Beat
    seconds per beat
    The beat tightens as you clear rounds. Start slow while the geometry is still new.
